{{Recipe}}

'''Roti jala''' are thin and lacy Malaysian pancakes. They are typically served—like other kinds of roti—with savory dishes like curries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Karim |first=Mehreen |date=2020-08-13 |title=I’ve Been Making Roti Jala Since I Was 10. You Can Too |url=https://www.bonappetit.com/story/roti-jala |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=Bon Appétit |language=en-US}}</ref> Many versions use coconut milk, but this one uses water.

== Ingredients ==
*4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Wheat Flour|wheat flour]]
*3 cups water
*2 standard [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] fine [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*A few drops of [[Cookbook:Food Coloring|food coloring]] (desired color; optional)

== Procedure ==

# Combine all the ingredients in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]], and blend until you get a well-combined batter. Over-blending will produce excess foam.
# Let the batter rest for 30 minutes.
# Transfer the batter to a squeeze-bottle with a nozzle (see notes).
# Heat a [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] over medium-high heat.
# If necessary, use a paper towel to lightly grease the pan with some oil.
# [[File:Roti jala penang.JPG|thumb|Shaping the pancake]]Use the squeeze bottle to drizzle batter over the surface of the pan in a swirling, lacy pattern.
# Let the pancake cook just until dry—avoid excessive coloration.
# Remove from the pan, transfer to a plate, and roll or fold up.
# Repeat the cooking process until you have used up all the batter.
# Serve warm.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* [[File:Roti jala tin cup 01.jpg|thumb|Specialized cup for making roti jala]]If you can get one, a specialized squeeze bottle with multiple nozzles will make it faster to shape the pancake. You can also use a specialized cup with multiple holes in the bottom.
